C1: Problem 1: Humanoid:MoveTo has an 8-second timeout. If the goal is not reached in about 8 s, MoveToFinished fires anyway with reached=false, so the zombie stops and you print 'arrived' without checking. Fix: read the boolean (local reached = hum.MoveToFinished:Wait()), and for long distances call MoveTo again on a loop or per waypoint, which resets the timer. Problem 2: MoveTo walks in a straight line with no pathfinding, so it hits walls. Fix: use PathfindingService:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentHeight=5, AgentCanJump=true}), path:ComputeAsync(start, goal) inside pcall, check path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success, then MoveTo each waypoint from path:GetWaypoints() in turn (Jump when waypoint.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump). Listen to path.Blocked and recompute, and recompute every so often for a moving target. Also set the NPC's network owner to the server (root:SetNetworkOwner(nil)) to avoid hitches.
C2: ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn defaults to true. On each respawn Roblox destroys the PlayerGui copy and clones a fresh one from StarterGui, so the LocalScript restarts and all its local variables reset to defaults. Fix: set ResetOnSpawn = false on that ScreenGui (the GUI and its script persist across deaths). Better still, keep settings state outside the GUI (a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage/PlayerScripts, or attributes on the Player) and, for persistence across sessions, send them to the server to save in a DataStore. Any references the script holds to the character must then be refreshed on CharacterAdded rather than captured once.
C3: Animations replicate from the client only when the client is the one allowed to animate that rig: its own character (the Animator under its Humanoid/AnimationController that the server created). Animation tracks played by a client on a server-owned NPC stay local, so nobody else sees the wave. An Animator created with Instance.new on the client only exists on that client, so the server and other players never even see it, and nothing it plays can replicate. Fix: play NPC animations from the server: a server Script loads the Animation via npc.Humanoid.Animator:LoadAnimation(anim) and :Play(). Make sure the Animator exists on the server (create it server-side or include it in the model). If a client triggers the wave, fire a RemoteEvent and let the server play it. Also the animation asset must be owned by the experience owner/group.
C4: (1) A Sound parented directly to Workspace (or SoundService) is non-positional: it plays at full volume everywhere. Parent it to a Part or Attachment at the barrel's position so it becomes 3D, set RollOffMode (InverseTapered) and RollOffMaxDistance. (2) Positional sounds fade based on RollOffMinDistance/RollOffMaxDistance and RollOffMode; raise RollOffMaxDistance (e.g. 500+), raise RollOffMinDistance so it stays loud longer, maybe use Linear/LinearSquare or InverseTapered, and increase Volume. (3) Loaded only fires when loading happens after you connect; if the sound is already loaded (IsLoaded true) Wait never returns. Use: if not siren.IsLoaded then siren.Loaded:Wait() end; siren:Play(). Optionally add a timeout, or ContentProvider:PreloadAsync.
C5:
workspace:Raycast's direction is a vector whose length IS the ray distance. .Unit makes it 1 stud long, so it nearly always misses and returns nil; you then index nil. And the ray starts inside the head, so it hits your own character. Fix:
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local dir = (mouseHit - head.Position).Unit * 500
local result = workspace:Raycast(head.Position, dir, params)
if result then print(result.Instance.Name, result.Position) end
Always nil-check the result. For a real gun, also do the authoritative raycast/validation on the server, not just the client.
C6: Two tweens on the same property of the same instance conflict: when a new tween on BackgroundTransparency plays, the running one is cancelled (the latest one wins), so the hover stops halfway, and when the flash ends it returns to a hardcoded value instead of the correct hover/normal state. Structure it as a small state machine: keep state flags (hovered, pressed), one function computeTarget() that returns the right transparency for the current state, and one helper that cancels the current tween for that property (store it, :Cancel()) and plays a new one to the target. MouseEnter/MouseLeave set hovered and call update; click flashes, then on Completed calls update() to go back to whatever the current state is (hovered or not). Alternatively, animate the flash on a different property/object (e.g. a UIStroke or overlay Frame) so the hover and click tweens never fight.

local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local DSS = game:GetService('DataStoreService')
local store = DSS:GetDataStore('PlayerData')
local PRODUCT_ID = 123
MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  if info.ProductId ~= PRODUCT_ID then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local ok = pcall(function()
    store:UpdateAsync('Player_' .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
      data = data or {Coins = 0, Receipts = {}}
      data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
      if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end
      data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = true
      data.Coins = (data.Coins or 0) + 500
      return data
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  -- update in-memory/leaderstats if player in game
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
Rules: set ProcessReceipt exactly once, in one server Script. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is saved; on any error or unknown product return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries (also on rejoin). Make it idempotent using PurchaseId (record it atomically with the grant) to prevent double grants. Don't yield forever; handler must not error. If you use session-cached data, grant into it and save, keeping receipt history pruned.

local DSS = game:GetService('DataStoreService')
local store = DSS:GetDataStore('Gems')
local function addGems(player, amount)
  assert(typeof(amount) == 'number' and amount == amount, 'bad amount')
  local key = 'Player_' .. player.UserId
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, result = pcall(function()
      return store:UpdateAsync(key, function(current)
        current = tonumber(current) or 0
        return current + amount
      end)
    end)
    if ok then return true, result end
    warn('addGems failed', attempt, result)
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false
end
Rules: the callback may run multiple times and must be pure and fast, with no yields (no waits, no other DataStore calls) and no side effects; return nil to cancel the write; handle nil for new keys; return a value that is serializable and under 4 MB. Wrap UpdateAsync in pcall, retry with backoff, respect budgets (GetRequestBudgetForRequestType), and only run on the server. Never trust amount from a client.

C13: Use MemoryStoreService, not DataStores. A MemoryStoreSortedMap (or MemoryStoreQueue) is built for fast, shared, temporary cross-server state: a sorted map keyed by userId with a sort key from skill/rating lets the matchmaker GetRangeAsync by skill band; a queue gives FIFO with ReadAsync/RemoveAsync and invisibility timeouts. Rules/limits: data is ephemeral with an expiration (max 45 days) so always set a TTL so stale entries vanish; memory quota is about 64 KB + 1 KB per user in the experience; request limits are about 1000 + 100 x concurrent users per minute; item size limit (32 KB value), key length limits. Wrap calls in pcall with retries and backoff. Use UpdateAsync for atomic changes, run a single matchmaker per region via a lock (or let each server claim entries atomically), remove players when they leave or teleport, then use TeleportService:ReserveServer + TeleportAsync to send groups. Use MessagingService only for notifications, not storage. DataStores are too slow, rate-limited and persistent for a queue.
C14: Server-side in the lobby: local code = TeleportService:ReserveServer(matchPlaceId) (or use TeleportOptions with ShouldReserveServer = true). Build TeleportOptions: options.ReservedServerAccessCode = code; options:SetTeleportData({matchId=...}). Then TeleportService:TeleportAsync(matchPlaceId, {p1,p2,p3,p4}, options) in pcall with retry, and handle TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed (retry or return players). Data: don't trust or rely on teleport data for coins/loadouts, it travels through the client and can be spoofed. Save each player's loadout and coins to the DataStore (or session-lock profile) and wait for the save before teleporting; the match server loads them from the DataStore on PlayerAdded. For non-sensitive match info, use teleport data via player:GetJoinData() on the server, or MemoryStore keyed by matchId. Pitfalls: teleports only from the server; ReserveServer and TeleportAsync can fail and are rate limited; destination must be in same universe; players may not all arrive, so handle timeouts/missing members; session locking to avoid save races; Studio cannot test teleports; preserve the access code if others need to join (store in MemoryStore).
C15: The client should only express intent: BuyItem:FireServer('Sword') (an item id). The server owns everything else: look up the price in a server-side catalog (ModuleScript in ServerStorage or shared read-only config), validate the argument type and that the item exists and is purchasable, check the player's server-held currency, check they don't already own it if unique, then subtract and grant atomically in server data and save. Never accept price, quantity, or currency amounts from the client. Add rate limiting/debounce per player, sanity-check all args (typeof, string length), and return a result via RemoteFunction or a follow-up event so the UI updates from server-replicated state (leaderstats/attributes) rather than client assumptions. The client may show prices for display only. Log suspicious requests.
C16: Use Roblox localization tables (LocalizationService). Enable automatic text capture/translation for static UI; upload or edit translations in the Creator Hub localization table for es, pt, de. For runtime strings, don't concatenate; use keys with parameters: entry key 'QuestCollect', source 'You collected {count} of {total} {item}'. In code: local translator = LocalizationService:GetTranslatorForPlayerAsync(player) (client: GetTranslatorForPlayerAsync(Players.LocalPlayer), in pcall) then label.Text = translator:FormatByKey('QuestCollect', {count=12, total=20, item=translator:Translate(game, 'apples')}) or use separate keys per item/plural. Set AutoLocalize = false on labels you fill manually so auto-translation doesn't double-translate. For NPC names, set AutoLocalize = false on those labels (or exclude them from the table / keep them out of translation) so they stay untranslated. Re-translate when the player's locale changes (translator.LocaleId / PropertyChangedSignal). Account for longer German text with TextScaled or AutomaticSize.
C17: Yes for the per-tick state. UnreliableRemoteEvent sends without ordering or delivery guarantees, so dropped packets aren't resent and don't block later ones, reducing latency and bandwidth spikes. That fits continuous steering/throttle and cosmetic exhaust data, where only the newest value matters. Rules: messages may be lost or arrive out of order (include a sequence number or timestamp and discard stale ones; interpolate on clients); payload is limited to about 900 bytes per call, larger ones are dropped, so keep it compact (e.g. buffers, quantized numbers); same FireServer/FireClient/FireAllClients API and same need for server validation; don't use it for important one-off events. Keep lap completion (and anything gameplay-critical) on a normal reliable RemoteEvent, and ideally compute laps on the server. Also consider lowering the rate and only sending changes.
C18: Unanchored parts near players get automatic network ownership: the server hands physics of the NPC to the nearest player's client. Each handoff (and the client's laggy simulation) causes the stutter, and the owning client can move/teleport the boss or fake its physics and Touched events. Fix: on the server, call SetNetworkOwner(nil) on the boss's root part (all its assemblies) after it spawns so the server always simulates it; check CanSetNetworkOwnership. Do damage checks on the server, not via client-ownable Touched: use server-side hitboxes (workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox/GetPartsInPart, OverlapParams, or magnitude checks) during attack windows with cooldowns; validate distances. Never trust client-reported hits. Reduce physics cost by keeping NPC parts minimal and Massless where appropriate.
C19: Put each turret's logic in an Actor: one Actor per turret (or batches, e.g. 6 Actors each handling 10 turrets) with a Script inside. In each script connect RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize()) and do the raycasts in parallel: workspace:Raycast is safe to call in parallel. Store results in local tables, then call task.synchronize() before writing to the DataModel (rotating the turret, setting properties, firing remotes, damaging Humanoids). Communicate via Actor:SendMessage / BindToMessageParallel or SharedTable. Restrictions: in the desynchronized phase you can read most properties but cannot write instance properties, create/destroy/parent instances, or call most yielding/unsafe APIs (only those marked Parallel Safe/Read Safe); scripts in different Actors don't share Luau state (each Actor has its own VM; module requires are separate copies), so use SharedTable or messages; instances must be descendants of the Actor to be modified by it safely. Batch work so each Actor gets enough to amortize overhead, and profile with the MicroProfiler. Reducing frequency (e.g. raycast at 10 Hz, stagger turrets) helps too.
C20: Before moving the character, the server should call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(targetPosition, timeout) in pcall so the region streams to that client, then PivotTo. Also consider character.PrimaryPart anchored briefly until the floor exists, or Workspace persistent models. For important structures like the dungeon entrance, set the Model's ModelStreamingMode to Atomic (streams as a whole) or Persistent (always present for all clients; use PersistentLoaded on Player) for spawn areas. On the client, use WaitForChild with timeouts and handle parts that may not exist. Settings: Workspace.StreamingMinRadius (lower for memory, but loaded guaranteed area), StreamingTargetRadius (lower to reduce memory on phones), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic so content streams out to free memory beyond target radius (default LowMemory only streams out under memory pressure), StreamingIntegrityMode (PauseOutsideLoadedArea / MinimumRadiusPause) so the character pauses instead of falling into unloaded areas. Use LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for distant models.
C21:
The Input Action System (IAS) is a set of instances: InputContext (a group of actions, can be enabled/disabled with Priority and Sink), containing InputAction (one gameplay action with a Type: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition), which contain InputBinding children mapping devices to the action (KeyCode, plus UIButton for touch buttons, and composite Up/Down/Left/Right keys for directions). Same action works across keyboard, gamepad and touch, and players can rebind. Reading Sprint (Bool action in a LocalScript):
local sprint = context:WaitForChild('Sprint')
sprint.Pressed:Connect(function() hum.WalkSpeed = 24 end)
sprint.Released:Connect(function() hum.WalkSpeed = 16 end)
-- or sprint.StateChanged:Connect(function(state) ... end) / sprint:GetState()
InputContext must be parented where the client sees it (e.g. under PlayerScripts/PlayerGui or ReplicatedStorage). 2026 change: Roblox moved the default PlayerModule character controls (movement, jump, camera) to be built on IAS, exposing their InputContexts/actions so developers can rebind or override default controls through IAS instead of forking ControlModule; forked old PlayerScripts may need updating. (Answered from memory, details may differ.)
C22: Legacy chat (LegacyChatService / the Lua chat system with ChatServiceRunner, ChatModules, forked Chat scripts) was deprecated and then retired in 2025: Roblox set a sunset deadline (around April 30, 2025) after which experiences were moved to TextChatService, and legacy chat no longer works/publishes. To revive: set TextChatService.ChatVersion = TextChatService, delete the forked Chat scripts (ChatServiceRunner, ChatScript, ChatModules) and any code using Chat:Chat or ChatService/SayMessageRequest remotes. Port customizations to TextChatService APIs: TextChannels (RBXGeneral, custom channels with TextChannel:AddUserAsync), OnIncomingMessage / OnBubbleAdded callbacks for tags/colors (TextChatMessageProperties), ShouldDeliverCallback for team/proximity chat, TextChatCommand for commands, ChatWindowConfiguration/ChatInputBarConfiguration/BubbleChatConfiguration for UI, TextChatService:DisplayBubble for NPC bubbles, TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage for system messages. Filtering is handled automatically.

C24: In January 2026 Roblox began requiring an age check (facial age estimation via Persona, or ID verification) to access chat globally. Users are placed in age groups (under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+), and can only chat with users in their own and adjacent groups unless they are Trusted Connections; under-9 chat is off by default; unverified users can't use chat. What to adjust: use TextChatService for all chat (legacy chat is gone) so the restrictions are enforced automatically; for any custom user-to-user text (signs, notes, custom chat UIs, DMs, party chat) check eligibility with TextChatService:CanUsersChatAsync / CanUsersDirectChatAsync (and CanUserChatAsync) and keep filtering via TextService. Expect players in the same server who can't talk to each other, so design social features (emotes, quick chat, gestures, voice-free cues) that work without chat, and don't build workarounds that let mismatched age groups exchange free text. Don't prompt users to move conversations off-platform. (From memory; check current docs for exact age bands.)
